To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have discovered a new type of linear magnetoresistance effect in topological insulators which is due to granularity and is not related to the topological nature of these materials.

We report on the correlation between the granularity controlled nonsaturating LMR and the mobility in granular films of topological insulator material Bi2Te3, and attribute the LMR to the classical mobility fluctuation effect.
we have found that the linear magnetoresistance is controlled by the granularity of the material.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the magnetotrans-port of granular films of Bi2Te3, an archetypal topological insulator, and the results are of general interest to the study of the magnetotranspor-tance of other small band gap semiconductors and topological insulators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LMR effect is universal for granular Bi2Se3 and Bi2Te3, and is attributed to the classical mobility fluctuation effect.
the LMR in Bi2Te3 is a classical effect and is a result of the mobility fluctuation.
the nonsaturating linear in field magnetoresistance in Bi2Te3 and other TI films is a result of classical mobility fluctuations, which are caused by the random nature of the grain size and shape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LMR effect in Bi2Te3 is a nonsaturating, classical, and mobility fluctuation induced magnetoresistance effect.
, the nonsaturating LMR effect in granular Bi2 Te3 films originates from the mobility fluctuation effect, and the LMR magnitude is determined by the average mobility of the films.
the LMR effect is not a unique property of TI materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LMR effect in TI materials is a nonsaturating phenomenon and can be tuned by controlling the film granularity.
the classical mobility fluctuation model is applicable to the nonsaturating LMR in granular TIs and small bandgap semiconductors.

the classical LMR effect can be used as a tool to characterize the granularity of a material, and the classical LMR theory can be applied to explain the LMR effect in TI films with different degree of granularities.
